_comment: Connector-specific edits a cli-printing-press reprint must NOT clobber. check_handfixes.py asserts every marker below is still present (and banned anti-patterns absent) and fails CI if a reprint dropped one. Provenance: issue #115 (reporter @AvlCompCo), fixed 2026-06-16. The fix is documentation + error-string only; no new flag/command. N-able removed the per-user 'API access' checkbox and moved to dedicated API Users; API Users still authenticate via the JSON-RPC Login method (partner=customer name, username=API-user login, password=API token -> visa), so COVE_PARTNER is REQUIRED for them. There is no bearer/header auth in the Cove API; the API token is the Login password, not a visa. Issue #133 (same reporter, on v0.1.2): clarified that COVE_PARTNER must be the FULL customer/partner string shown in the Cove console customer dropdown (usually including the account email in parentheses, e.g. 'Acme Corp (admin@acme.com)'), not just the company name -- Cove returns the same 2100 error for a wrong COVE_PARTNER format as for a bad password; and decoded the 13501 'Operation failed because of security reasons' visa error (the API User's role may not permit the method) while documenting that the raw generated endpoint commands need an explicit --visa "$(cove-cli auth token)" and that `cove-cli call <Method>` injects it automatically. Documentation + error-string only; no new flag/command.

handfixes.summary: doctor probes a real GET endpoint with the real credential and refuses to dial a placeholder base_url, instead of calling any HTTP response 'reachable' and never checking the credential
handfixes.why: `doctor` is the command every SKILL, guide and docs page tells an operator to run to confirm the connector works, and it could not tell a working install from a broken one. It called any HTTP response to `GET /` "reachable" and rendered it green, so a base_url aimed at the vendor's web UI (where every API path 404s) and a token rejected with 401 on every call both produced an all-green report. On this connector family it also never probed the credential at all: it printed "present, not verified" and left the operator to guess. The mirror defect: a connector whose shipped base_url default is a placeholder dialled the placeholder host, and the DNS failure rendered as "FAIL API: unreachable" - telling a correctly-credentialled operator they were broken without naming the one variable that would fix it. Several placeholder hosts resolve through live wildcard DNS and answer real HTTP, so dialling one produced a confident green verdict against a stranger's server. Measured and gated by tools/maintainer/check_doctor_truth.py. See issue #282.

asserts.contains: report["credentials"] = "ERROR not verified: no credential is configured, so nothing was probed."
report["api"] = "not configured (base_url is a placeholder); set " + doctorBaseURLEnv + " to your own instance URL"

handfixes.summary: every operator credential this connector reads is declared on all three install channels: manifest.json (.mcpb), server.json (MCP Registry) and mcp-install.md (manual install)
handfixes.why: Issue #282 ('three live-verified connectors prompt for the wrong credentials'). A connector is installed through THREE independent channels that each carry their own copy of the credential list: manifest.json server.mcp_config.env (what the .mcpb bundle hands Claude Desktop, which has no shell profile, no config.toml and no export - so an undeclared variable is a variable nobody is ever asked for), server.json environmentVariables (the MCP Registry publish channel), and mcp-install.md's copy-paste JSON blocks plus its remote launch line (the manual path, which never touches the bundle at all). The fleet-wide audit found 60 of 65 connectors under-declaring 122 operator-facing variables in the manifest, 61 of 65 mcp-install.md pages omitting 125, and hudu's server.json missing the base URL its manifest marks required. For cove the manifest gained: COVE_BASE_URL, COVE_PARTNER, COVE_PASSWORD, COVE_USERNAME. server.json gained: COVE_BASE_URL, COVE_PARTNER, COVE_PASSWORD, COVE_USERNAME. mcp-install.md's env blocks gained: COVE_BASE_URL. manifest.json, server.json and mcp-install.md are ALL regenerated by /msp-skills-publish on an UPDATE or re-onboard, so without this ledger a regeneration silently drops every declaration and CI stays green (check_env_schema.py is wired --warn). The asserts below name the specific credentials, not a count, so dropping one and adding another cannot cancel out. REPRINT 4.34.0 (2026-10-24): the press adds PRINTING_PRESS_CLIENT_PROFILE, COVE_MCP_READ_ONLY, COVE_NO_LOCAL_DATA, COVE_MCP_HTTP_TOKEN and COVE_USER_AGENT; all five are declared on the three channels and pinned here.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: cli-printing-press should emit server.mcp_config.env, the matching user_config prompts, server.json environmentVariables and mcp-install.md's env blocks from ONE declaration of the connector's operator-facing environment, so the three channels cannot be generated out of step. Until then check_env_schema.py compares all three and this ledger pins them.

handfixes.summary: A redirect that leaves the origin (another host:port, or https down to http) carries no credential: every credential header and every config-file header is stripped, and a hop that would replay a request body (307/308 of a non-GET) is refused
handfixes.why: tools/maintainer/class_harness.py auth-wire found cove sending nothing the harness could see, because doctor never logged in; the JSON-RPC client (coverpc) followed a 307 with the password or visa in the body to a second server on a 307. The generated CheckRedirect deleted only the primary auth header on a cross-host hop; Go itself strips Authorization and Cookie only when the hostname changes (a port change keeps them), never strips a custom header, and replays the body on a 307 or 308, which for a token request is the client secret. Same-origin hops still re-derive auth (ninjaone precedent); a non-GET hop off the origin is refused rather than replayed (connectsecure precedent). The unit tests call the client's real CheckRedirect with every header Go copies onto the next hop and fail on the generated code. The origin compares like a URL: hostnames case-insensitively and an explicit default port as none (Codex review round 1: an upper-case base URL refused a healthy same-origin redirect). Hosts compare the way the network resolves them: an IP literal by address with its IPv6 zone exact, a DNS name ASCII case-insensitively, a non-ASCII name exactly (Codex review round 2: case-folding the zone let fe80::1%LAN0 pass for fe80::1%lan0).
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: client.go.tmpl CheckRedirect should strip every credential header (the primary, composed siblings and config-file headers) on any hop that leaves the origin, compare host:port and scheme, and refuse to replay a body off the origin; a hand-written auth client should get the same CheckRedirect.

handfixes.summary: doctor reports Cove's real auth scheme (JSON-RPC Login with COVE_PARTNER, COVE_USERNAME, COVE_PASSWORD) and, when those are set, performs one Login and reports the verdict by Cove error number only, instead of 'auth: not required' and 'no credential is configured'
handfixes.why: The generated doctor had no model of the JSON-RPC visa login, so with all three credentials set it reported auth as not required and the credential as not configured, and probed only a credential-free GET: it could not tell a working install from a wrong password, and the auth-wire class saw no credential on the wire at all. The Login probe uses the same coverpc client every real command uses (with its cross-origin redirect refusal), never caches a session, and never prints the server's response text, so nothing the server reflects reaches the report. TestCoveDoctorLoginVerdict covers an accepted login, a refusal and a non-Cove error page, each reflecting the password, and fails if the verdict carries server text. Without COVE_* set (check_doctor_truth.py's auth_header states) the generated path is unchanged.

handfixes.summary: doctor reports a host whose reachability answer was withheld (it repeated a held credential) as reachable and still runs the Login probe, instead of calling it unreachable and skipping the credential check
handfixes.why: The 4.34.0 reprint routes every answer through the client's one exit point (coveExit), which refuses an answer that repeats a held credential with ErrCoveAnswerWithheld. The generated doctor read that error as a network failure: it reported 'unreachable' for a host that had answered and skipped the Login, so no credential was ever checked (class_harness.py auth-wire failed on PR #473; main's cove reported reachable and sent the Login). A withheld answer is a reached host. TestDoctorWithheldReachAnswerStillRunsTheLogin drives doctor against a host whose reachability answer repeats the password and fails without the fix.

handfixes.summary: One decoded output funnel for every server text the client shows: maskCredentialText (every API error, transport error, displayed URL and --dry-run parameter goes through it) still masks each held credential as written and URL-escaped, then withholds the WHOLE text if any held value survives in any view reachable by undoing control/format characters, JSON and JavaScript escapes, percent escapes at any depth, HTML entities, markup tags, and base64/base64url/hex runs at every alignment (cliutil.FunnelWithhold, shared byte-identical across the fleet). The held set is every value the masks cover plus the part after a scheme word and both halves of a base64 id:secret pair (Basic auth, composed keys). Surfaces funnelled here: the API error body (checked whole before the 4096-byte display cut, then again as shown). This connector also holds COVE_PASSWORD (read from the environment outside Config), and its hand-written JSON-RPC client (internal/coverpc) funnels every server text it shows: a non-200 answer and an unparseable answer are checked whole before the 300-byte cut and again as shown, a JSON-RPC error message is withheld when the answer echoes a held value, and a transport error that echoes one is withheld; the held values are the API token (Password) and the session visa. Round 3 (owner-approved structural pass): the decoder searches every view breadth-first over one fixed set of steps (control-character drop, JSON and JavaScript escapes, the identity escape as its own step, percent, HTML entities, tag strip, base64 at four alignments, hex at two), matches every view, the original included, before any filter, keeps every view a step makes (a literal backslash survives), deduplicates, and is capped by total work (512 times the input plus 4 MiB; text over 1 MiB or past the cap is withheld). Every value a funnel call is given is held process-wide (cliutil.FunnelHold), and the client holds its credentials when built and its resolved auth header on every request. Two error-only backstops withhold any held value: every command error before Cobra prints it plus every JSON/agent error envelope (internal/cli/secret_funnel_cli.go), and every MCP error result and handler error through the outermost tool middleware (cmd/<mcp>/secret_funnel_mcp.go). Success output is never funnelled.
handfixes.why: class_harness.py secret-echo (Step 3.1, PR #436) drives the built CLI and MCP server against a fake server that reflects each configured credential in every encoding; on origin/main this connector printed the credential HTML-entity-encoded, JSON-escaped, double URL-encoded or base64 (the generated masks cover only the raw, QueryEscape and PathEscape forms; press issue #5145). Matching encoded needles one at a time never converged (saas-alerts and cisco-meraki review loops), so the fix is a decode-then-check backstop that withholds the whole text and fails closed (text over 4 MiB, a decoding chain that does not settle in 32 rounds, or work past the budget is withheld). Classification is kept: the plain withheld notice avoids every word the auth-error classifiers match, and a withheld text that itself read as an auth failure gets a notice that says so (an HTTP 400 'invalid token' answer echoing the token keeps its auth exit code). Codex round 1 (2026-10-23) added that, the fail-closed depth bound (a text-like layer left at depth 8 withholds), the JavaScript escapes \v, \0 and the identity escape, a bounded \u{ search, and the token-endpoint error bodies outside the client. Known limits: values under 8 characters are only masked as written; case-changed, split-and-interleaved or otherwise transformed (compressed, encrypted) echoes are not reconstructed. A reprint that drops these edits fails class_harness.py secret-echo in CI and these asserts.
handfixes.spec_encode_followup: Press-side: cli-printing-press issue #5145 (encoded credential echo). The generated maskCredentialText should end in a decode-then-check backstop over every held credential, and the error-body and token-endpoint paths should check the whole body before the display cut.

handfixes.summary: doctor treats Cove's one global API host as a real endpoint, not the shipped placeholder, so a correctly configured install runs the Login probe
handfixes.why: The doctor-verdict template set doctorShippedBaseURL to the connector's shipped base_url. Cove has one global host (https://api.backup.management), so every correctly configured install printed 'ERROR base_url is still the shipped placeholder' and never ran the credential probe. The shipped placeholder is empty for Cove. A reprint or the doctor-verdict replay restores the old constant.

handfixes.summary: the hand-written JSON-RPC client waits on the press 4.34.0 rate limiter with the request context
handfixes.why: Press 4.34.0's AdaptiveLimiter.Wait takes a context: a cancelled command stops instead of sleeping. The shipped coverpc.go called Wait() with no context and does not compile on 4.34.0; replaying it restores that.

handfixes.summary: authErr (exit code 4) is defined by hand, since press 4.34.0 omits it for a spec whose auth type is none
handfixes.why: Every hand-written Cove command reports a credential failure with exit code 4 through authErr. Cove's login lives outside the press auth model (spec auth: none), so 4.34.0 no longer generates authErr; without this the hand commands do not compile.

asserts.contains: func authErr(err error) error { return &cliError{code: 4, err: err} }

handfixes.summary: call sends only Get and Enumerate methods unless --yes; over MCP --yes is refused, so call only reads there
handfixes.why: call takes any JSON-RPC method name, including ones that change the tenant. A write needs the operator's explicit --yes.

handfixes.summary: no credential-bearing JSON-RPC call goes to a non-loopback http:// host, and the cached visa is bound to endpoint, partner and username
handfixes.why: The JSON-RPC client is hand-written, so the generated client's plaintext guard does not cover it; an unbound cached visa could be replayed against another tenant or endpoint.

handfixes.summary: the generated client's plaintext and redirect-replay guards count a JSON body member named visa as a credential
handfixes.why: Raw generated endpoint commands carry the Cove session visa in the JSON-RPC body (--visa), which the generated guards did not recognise as a secret.

handfixes.summary: credentials shorter than the canonical funnel's minimum are withheld in every stacked encoding; success data is checked scalar by scalar; a returned visa is found by its decoded JSON member name and held before any text is shown; wired from cove-only files so the canonical funnel copies stay byte-identical
handfixes.why: The fleet funnel skips short values, never checks success results, and the Cove visa arrives in the response body. Codex rounds 1 and 2 on the 4.34.0 reprint found a short password shown double-base64, a numeric password echoed in a success result, and a visa under an escaped member name. apply_secret_funnel.py rewrites the canonical funnel files, so the cove wiring lives in cove_short_funnel_cli.go and cove_short_funnel_mcp.go. Codex review round 1: the generated client base64-wrapped a binary success body before the visa check and showed a fresh visa from an HTTP error body; every response now holds its visas at read time, every success body is checked before wrapping, caching or replay, and the dry-run body preview is masked. Codex review round 2 and the round 2 adversarial review: response header values reached a result (Content-Type) or an error (Content-Encoding, cf-mitigated, X-Request-ID), and a visa after another name/value pair escaped the regex fallback. Now the generated client has one exit point (coveExit) that checks the whole returned value and every error, holds the visas of every header and of the raw body before any decoding, and never quotes a response header value; visa discovery is one scanner that starts at every 'visa' name and holds only values with the visa shape (RFC 6750 b64token, 16+ characters), so a word next to 'visa' is never held.
